items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: Jerry Hey is one of my horn arranging heroes

ctx.x: What do you get — do you get a recording and a lead sheet or what?

Sometimes I do it by ear, sometimes I write out the parts. It just depends on the complexity. But once again unison is always the strongest horn voicing when you have a small horn section. Jerry Hey is one of my horn arranging heroes — Michael Jackson, Earth, Wind & Fire, Brothers Johnson, Quincy Jones, Al Jarreau — particularly Al Jarreau “High Crime,” that album. And once again it’s that horn unison with the, you know the tenor and the trombone an octave below the trumpets. And sometimes he’s got the trumpets…
Okay so it makes me think of a tune. See if you can name this tune, speaking of unison horns (scats).

items.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023
items.q: I had a conversation with Tom “Bones” Malone recently and he said the idea is you don’t conflict with the vocal

ctx.x: I had a conversation with Tom “Bones” Malone recently and he said the idea is you don’t conflict with the vocal because it’s the most important thing. I’m just putting horns on
and make sure that they occur in their own space because I’m just the frosting on the cake.
